source.title: Soft ascent-descent as a stable and flexible alternative to flooding

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Compares training procedures and reports training-to-test loss gaps and test performance, using a different intervention from the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper tests SoftAD, Flooding, SAM, and ERM; no listed version directly covers these methods. It also discusses sharpness and prior findings, but those cited findings are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares loss objectives and training procedures, but its own results do not test V1–V8. SAM performance and theoretical links to gradient regularization do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or its correlation with generalization gaps. Adam and SGD are used on different tasks, without a controlled optimizer comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that concentrating individual losses around a threshold through SoftAD can balance test loss and accuracy and produce smaller model norms, interpreted as implicit regularization. Threshold selection remains unresolved. Their universal smallest-gap statement holds for Table 1's four methods, but the added iFlood comparisons have exceptions.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces SoftAD, a pointwise smooth ascent-descent loss wrapper, and compares it with ERM, Flooding, SAM, and iFlood; it does not use the interventions in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that trends in the linear-model experiment change with mini-batch size; validation-selected threshold values also differ by method and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: SoftAD has the smallest final cross-entropy loss gap among ERM, Flooding, SAM, and SoftAD on all seven Table 1 datasets. In Table 3 it improves on ERM everywhere, but iFlood has smaller gaps on CIFAR-100 (2.558 versus 2.696) and FashionMNIST (0.273 versus 0.463).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Validation-selected SoftAD can reduce the final cross-entropy generalization gap relative to ERM and several alternative loss-training procedures; superiority depends on the comparator and dataset.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are given for Table 1 or Table 3 gaps. The thresholds are validation-selected, and the authors state that how to set the threshold remains unanswered. Some reported comparisons are presented only in figures; they are not quantified here.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out from the numeric generalization-gap results in Tables 1 and 3. Figure-only trajectories and qualitative test-accuracy and model-norm comparisons were not converted into numeric rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the paired natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected models on the same image task, including local connectivity and initialization effects.
Controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons and tuning or recovery conditions.
A large-batch held-out performance penalty under fixed epochs and its recovery through recipe changes.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on training-set size, strength, or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with error gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm and margin measures.
Memorization-based example removal versus matched random removal and subsequent test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded gap values and numerical baselines match the supplied tables. These are method-performance rows outside V1–V8, rather than evidence supporting or challenging those versions. The mini-batch sensitivity statement in C.3 gives no directional large-batch penalty establishing V5. Epoch-wise double descent is not a width sweep establishing V2. Smaller parameter norms and SAM training do not establish V7. Figure-only results are already declared in rows_left_out, and no omitted result tests a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and the specified architectures.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons under the specified tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout addition and removal, including the specified training-set and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Identification and removal of memorized examples.
